evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: 形義通解; bronze forms; Shuowen and Guangyun entries
evidence.text: This source proposes that bronze 次 shows an open-mouthed person and two marks interpreted cautiously as saliva; it may be an early form of 咨, with an original sense of consulting or deliberating. It reports that in late Spring and Autumn forms the two marks move below 欠 or become short horizontal strokes, and that Chu slips sometimes use 次 for 即 or 節. Its reading of the marks and original sense is an interpretation, not an established fact. It also gives the Shuowen account 不前不精也。从欠，二聲 and Guangyun fanqie 七四切.
evidence.kind: modern paleographic analysis and historical dictionary record
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 次

evidence.field: character evolution and cited inscription inventory
evidence.text: The page lists oracle-bone examples including 合7361 and 合5814, Western Zhou bronze examples including 集成1354 (史次鼎), and later bronze, Qin slip, seal, clerical and regular-script examples. Its analysis treats the oracle graph as a composite indicator: a component identified as 師’s initial form plus two strokes indicating a military encampment; it describes later bronze forms as 欠 plus 二 phonetic. This conflicts with CUHK’s interpretation of the bronze points as saliva and with accounts rejecting 二 as the original part.
evidence.title: 次字形演变字源

evidence.field: 字形; historical semantic account; 声系
evidence.text: This dictionary interprets the graph as a person sighing or lamenting, with escaping breath; it rejects 二 as a component of the original graph and says the Shuowen definition and analysis are unclear. It suggests later ‘second/order’ senses may derive from repetition and treats the military lodging sense as use by sound of a graph associated with a military station. These are dictionary proposals; the semantic bridges are not demonstrated in this entry. It records later meanings including lament, consultation, succession/order, lodging and encampment.
evidence.title: 次(ジ)とは？ 意味や使い方 — コトバンク

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.field: dated textual attestations and semantic development
evidence.text: The entry cites Warring States bamboo slips and Han silk manuscripts for ‘inferior/next in rank’ or ‘in sequence’: Shuihudi Qin slips, 語書 slip 8, give 以次傳; Mawangdui Laozi A, line 124 (Han manuscript), repeats 其次 for successive ranks. It separately reports a Han silk use written 次 for 恣 (‘indulge’) and a Mawangdui Xici use written 次 where the transmitted Zhouyi has 濟, presenting these as graphic loans/usages, not stages of the graph’s formation. It cites Zuozhuan 僖公元年 for troops lodging at 聶北 and Zhouli 掌次 for temporary tents, but gives no date for those transmitted textual witnesses in the entry. It traces ordered/serial senses with later literary examples (Liu Yuxi and Bai Juyi) without establishing a precise first occurrence.
evidence.kind: historical sense attestations and dictionary analysis
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 次

evidence.field: Glyph origin; historical pronunciation; modern readings
evidence.text: The entry reports a recent proposal attributed to Zhang (2024): bronze graphic connections with 即 may support an Old Chinese initial *tsʰ-, with a tentative reconstruction /*tsʰik-s/. It says older proposals connecting 次 with 二 (*njis ‘two’), including Pulleyblank (1962) and Sagart and Baxter (2012), are untenable in light of paleographic evidence. This is a secondary summary of a disputed proposal, not direct inspection of Zhang’s article. The entry gives Standard Mandarin cì (Pinyin) and Cantonese ci3 (Jyutping); another entry page lists Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese /*[s-n̥]i[j]-s/ and Zhengzhang /*sn̥ʰis/ for 次, illustrating disagreement among reconstruction systems. No proposed component pronunciation needs to be asserted here because the phonetic status of 二 is contested.
evidence.kind: secondary summary of disputed paleographic and phonological analyses
evidence.title: 次 — Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: The entry identifies Japanese つぎ (tsugi) as a nominalization of the continuative form of 次ぐ (tsugu, ‘follow; be next’), and gives Tokyo pronunciation [tsɨɡʲi]. This supports a Japanese word-history account, not a Japanese origin for the Chinese graph. No early Japanese attestation was verified in the inspected material.
evidence.title: 次 — Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: Kotobank, 精選版 日本国語大辞典
evidence.text: For the Japanese Sino-Japanese reading じ, the entry dates a noun use meaning ‘order’ to 空華日用工夫略集, dated 1382-12-09. This is a dated Japanese attestation, distinct from the earlier history of the Chinese graph or its senses.
evidence.title: 次(ジ)とは？ 意味や使い方 — コトバンク

evidence.field: Shuowen, Guangyun, graph history, dated textual examples
evidence.text: The page records Shuowen's 不前不精也。从欠，二聲 and 七四切, and Guangyun fanqie 七四. Its modern analysis interprets bronze 次 as 欠 with two marks, tentatively read as saliva, and proposes that it may be an early form of 咨 with a consult/deliberate sense. It reports that in late Spring and Autumn examples the marks move below 欠 or become short strokes. It cites Shuihudi Qin slips, 語書 slip 8, 以次傳 and Mawangdui Laozi A, line 124, 其次 for ordered or ranked senses; Mawangdui silk uses 次 for 恣 and 濟 in separate loan usages. It also cites transmitted Zhouli and Zuozhuan passages for tent/lodging meanings, without dating the textual witnesses.

evidence.field: Historical form inventory and formation analysis
evidence.text: The page lists oracle examples (including 合7361 and 合5814), Western Zhou bronze 集成1354 (史次鼎), later bronze, Qin slip, seal, clerical, and regular-script samples. It interprets the oracle graph as a military sign composed of a form it identifies as an early 師 plus strokes indicating a station. For bronze and later forms it analyzes 欠 plus 二 as semantic and phonetic, respectively. This is one modern analysis and conflicts with the CUHK saliva/speech interpretation and other accounts rejecting 二 in the original graph.

evidence.field: Glyph origin, contested sound analysis, modern readings
evidence.text: The inspected entry presents an exhaling-person account, tentatively connecting the graph to 咨, while saying Shuowen's 二-plus-欠 analysis is refuted by early forms. It also reports a Zhang (2024) proposal of graphic connections between bronze 次 and 即, with tentative Old Chinese /*tsʰik-s/. This is a secondary summary; the article itself was not inspected. The entry gives Standard Mandarin cì in Pinyin, Cantonese ci3 in Jyutping, and Zhengzhang Old Chinese 次 *sn̥ʰis; the dossier separately records Baxter–Sagart *[s-n̥]i[j]-s and Middle Chinese tshijH. These reconstructions belong to distinct systems and do not establish 二's role as a sound component.
evidence.kind: secondary summary of disputed paleographic and phonological analyses
evidence.title: 次 — Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.field: Modern readings, proposed components, historical pronunciation
evidence.text: The entry lists Mandarin cì (Pinyin), labels 二 as both a sound and meaning component, and supplies Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese 次 *[s-n̥]i[j]-s and 二 *[n]i[j]-s, with Middle Chinese 次 tshijH. Its component analysis is a modern proposal, not independent confirmation of the disputed phonetic role; its historical glyph sequence labels examples oracle, early Western Zhou bronze, Shuowen seal, and Eastern Han clerical.

These are modern vector redrawings based on historical character sources, not photographs of artifacts.

gaps: The modern analyses disagree about the earliest graph: military station marker, human breathing/sighing, or a speaking/lamenting figure. The inspected textual descriptions do not resolve this; no glyph image was visually inspected.

The proposed early reading of the oracle form and semantic links from an alleged original ‘consult/deliberate’ or ‘encampment’ sense to later ‘second/order’ remain uncertain. Available evidence does not establish a dated first attestation of each sense or a continuous semantic development.

Shuowen’s 欠 + 二 phonetic analysis is a historical account, contradicted by several modern paleographic interpretations. Its classification of 二 as phonetic is not independently established by the inspected material. A 2024 proposal associates bronze forms graphically with 即, but its primary publication was not inspected.

No independent sound component reading for 二 was established, and the phonetic role of 二 remains disputed. Old Chinese reconstructions for 次 differ by system; the tentative Zhang reconstruction is reported secondhand.

The whole-graph loan idea for the military lodging sense is not securely demonstrated: the inspected sources propose sound borrowing from another graph, but the origin word’s pronunciation and precise relationship are not established here. No depicted tool or weapon is implicated.

The available date for the military lodging quotation is the transmitted Zuozhuan passage attribution; the inspected source did not date its textual witness. Earliest attestations for the lodging/tent senses, ‘next/second’, and several extensions therefore remain open.

Japanese kun reading つぎ is described as native lexical material related to 次ぐ, while Japanese じ is a Sino-Japanese reading. The inspected sources do not establish first attestation dates for these Japanese forms.

The earliest graph's interpretation remains disputed: CUHK reads bronze marks with 欠 as possible saliva and relates the graph tentatively to 咨; 39017 reads oracle forms as a military station sign; another account reads a person exhaling. Inspected descriptions do not settle these alternatives, and no glyph pixels were visually inspected in this research stage.

The bronze transition from two points to marks below 欠 or short horizontal strokes is reported by CUHK, but the inspected material does not establish whether this is graphic corruption, regularization, or a meaningful change.

Shuowen's 欠 plus 二 phonetic analysis is historically important but is not independently established by the inspected paleographic evidence. Sources proposing 二 as phonetic do not supply a secure component-reading comparison within a single reconstruction system sufficient to settle the matter.

Mandarin cì, Cantonese ci3, Middle Chinese tshijH, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[s-n̥]i[j]-s, Zhengzhang *sn̥ʰis, and the secondary-reported Zhang /*tsʰik-s/ are distinct language/period or reconstruction-system records; the sources disagree on Old Chinese onset and the phonetic role of 二. No independent original referent/name is established for the contested earliest graph; no borrowing claim requiring a depicted tool or weapon is supported.

Qin and Han manuscript citations provide dated evidence for ordered/ranked 次 uses and separate graphic loans 次-for-恣 and 次-for-濟. The citations do not prove a semantic chronology from an alleged original sense. Tent/lodging and military encampment examples are cited from transmitted texts without a dated textual witness in the inspected entry, and first attestations or semantic bridges to rank/order are unresolved.

No character-specific reusable historical 次 glyph image was verified. Commons searches surfaced unrelated file pages; the Sinica record is a useful artifact-linked lead but reuse terms and a direct image URL were not verified. Commons photograph candidate open failed, so it is excluded. No glyph image was visually inspected.
